name: gdc-rebc-thyr
alternateName: Comprehensive genomic characterization of radiation-related papillary thyroid cancer in the Ukraine
description:
This cohort characterises papillary thyroid carcinoma arising in people who were children or in utero in Ukraine at the time of the 1986 Chernobyl accident, and it exists because no comparable exposure can ethically be reconstructed. Whole genome sequencing is available on 395 cases, RNA sequencing on 438 and microRNA on 437. The scientific question it was built for - what radiation does to a genome, and whether the resulting tumors differ mechanistically from sporadic ones - is answerable here and almost nowhere else.
It is also an object lesson in why a catalog entry is not enough. The harmonized clinical records report a median follow-up of 115 months - but that median rests on just 12 of the 449 cases. They also record vital status for 440 of 449 cases as "not reported". A researcher who selected this dataset on the strength of its follow-up figure would discover only after obtaining access that no survival analysis is possible, and that the follow-up figure itself rests on under 3% of the cohort.
citeAs: Radiation-related genomic profile of papillary thyroid carcinoma after the Chernobyl accident

supportedQuestions: What is the mutational and structural signature of ionising radiation exposure in a solid human tumor, and how does it scale with dose?
Do radiation-associated papillary thyroid carcinomas differ transcriptionally from sporadic ones, and can a classifier separate them?
Does age at exposure shape the resulting tumor genome, given that participants were children or in utero at the time?
Can microRNA profiles discriminate radiation-associated thyroid tumors, as a cheaper assay than whole genome sequencing for future screening cohorts?

blockingLimitations.statement: Vital status is populated for 98% of cases and informative for 0%: every populated value is "not reported". A follow-up time is derivable for just 12 of 449 cases, and even for those there is no outcome to pair it with, so no survival endpoint exists. No survival analysis of any kind is possible.

Individual reconstructed radiation dose is not present in the harmonized clinical records, although it is the variable that distinguishes this cohort from any other thyroid cancer resource and is analyzed in the marker paper.
rulesOut: Any claim about radiation dose thresholds

inappropriateUses: Survival or prognostic analysis of any kind.
Quantifying cancer risk attributable to Chernobyl exposure.
